newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Enron unit signs power deal with Indonesia.
newsitem.headline: Enron unit signs power deal with Indonesia.

text.p: PT East Java Power Corp, 50.1 percent owned by Enron Corp, said it signed a 20-year agreement on Monday to sell electricity to Indonesia's state-owned power company PT Perusahaan Listrik Negara (PLN).
PLN officials said the company will pay 5.76 U.S. cents per kilowatt hour for electricity supplied by PT East Java.
Enron official Robert Baldwin said the electricity to be sold to PLN would come from a $508 million 500-megawatt gas-fired plant to be built in East Java.
Construction is expected to begin in the fourth quarter of next year and is scheduled to be operational by the year 2000.
"I think the large market in Asia, across China, India and Indonesia, have tremendous opportunities for a company like ours," he told reporters.
"The (sale) price we think is the lowest that has been agreed so far between private companies and PLN...and it will be good for us, PLN and PLN customers," Baldwin said.
Enron's partners in PT East Java are Pasuruan Power Co of Indonesia which has a 25-percent stake and Prince Holdings Ltd of Hong Kong with 24.9 percent.
